subject: Art & Design
title: Streetwear: How Skate Culture Became Luxury
description: Learn Streetwear: How Skate Culture Became Luxury in one minute.

hook.text: A Supreme brick sold for $30. A box-logo t-shirt resells for $1,000. Streetwear turned scarcity into religion.

buildup.text: Streetwear emerged from 1990s skate, surf, and hip-hop culture: graphic tees, hoodies, sneakers, and limited drops.

discovery.text: James Jebbia (Supreme), Shawn Stussy, and Nigo (A Bathing Ape) built brands on authenticity, community.

twist.text: Luxury brands initially mocked streetwear. Then Louis Vuitton × Supreme happened (2017). The hierarchy collapsed.

climax.text: Streetwear rewrote fashion's business model: drop culture, resale markets.

punchline.text: Streetwear didn't climb the fashion ladder. It built its own.

quiz.question: How did streetwear change fashion's traditional business model?
options: It replaced seasonal collections with limited drops, resale markets, and hype culture
It made all fashion free and accessible
It eliminated the need for physical stores

details.summary: Streetwear emerged from 1980s skate and surf culture in California, with brands like Stüssy and Supreme producing limited-edition graphic tees and hoodies.
details.whyItMatters: Streetwear's rise to luxury status represents the biggest power shift in fashion history — from top-down haute couture to bottom-up street culture. It proved authenticity and community matter more than heritage.
takeaways: Streetwear emerged from 1980s skate and surf culture
Supreme and Stüssy pioneered limited-edition drop culture
Virgil Abloh's Louis Vuitton role symbolized the power shift

faq.question: What makes streetwear different from regular casual clothing?
faq.answer: Streetwear is defined by limited releases (drops), community-driven hype, graphic-heavy design, and roots in subcultures like skateboarding, hip-hop, and graffiti. The scarcity model and cultural authenticity create value beyond the garment itself.

faq.question: Why did luxury brands embrace streetwear?
faq.answer: Traditional luxury was losing relevance with younger consumers who valued cultural credibility over heritage. Collaborations with streetwear brands (Louis Vuitton x Supreme, Dior x Nike) brought youth energy, social media buzz, and new customers to aging luxury houses.
